---
title: "From the Hoppe urn to stick-breaking"
subtitle: "Catalog P-06 · rung 5 · after Broderick (MLSS 2016, part II)"
description: "An urn with one black ball of mass alpha grows new colours; the colour shares settle down to stick-breaking weights, and the first colour's share is Beta(1, alpha)."
toc: false
---

Put one black ball of mass alpha in an urn. Draw a ball with probability proportional to
its mass. If it is the black ball, put it back together with a ball of a *new* colour. If it
is a coloured ball, put it back with one more ball of the *same* colour. After n draws there
are n coloured balls, and the chance that the next draw brings a new colour is
alpha / (alpha + n). This is Hoppe's urn, and it is the [Chinese restaurant
process](crp.qmd) with colours for tables.

```{=html}
<div id="w-urn" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/hoppe-urn.js"></script>
<script>
  window.__dpxUrn = DPX["hoppe-urn"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-urn"), {});
</script>
```

## What to try

- **Step** (or Enter) a few times and follow the step strip: the first draw must take the
  black ball, so the first colour appears at once.
- **+100, auto.** The colour shares stop moving much after a few hundred draws. The bar is
  one draw of stick-breaking weights, in the order the colours appeared (the same colours as
  the [stick-breaking](stick-breaking.qmd) widget).
- **Repeat 1000 times.** A thousand fresh urns: the first colour's share lines up with the
  Beta(1, alpha) density. That is the first stick-breaking piece, and the share of the cluster
  a randomly chosen unit belongs to, W_SB, has the same Beta(1, alpha) distribution given
  alpha.
- **alpha.** A small alpha keeps one colour dominant; a large alpha keeps opening new ones.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
After Broderick (MLSS 2016, part II); the mathematics is re-implemented and no code is copied.
:::
